title: Electric Planes Move Closer to Carrying Passengers in the US
summaryZh: 美國電動飛機加速發展，業者盼2028洛杉磯奧運前推出空中計程車。
summaryHi: अमेरिका में इलेक्ट्रिक विमान आगे बढ़ रहे हैं, 2028 तक एयर टैक्सी की उम्मीद।
summaryEs: Los aviones eléctricos avanzan en EE. UU. y podrían llevar pasajeros en 2028.
summaryJa: 米国で電動航空機の開発が加速、2028年までに空飛ぶタクシー実現目指す。
summaryKo: 미국에서 전기 항공기 개발이 속도를 내며 2028년 에어택시를 목표로 한다.
summaryEn: US electric aircraft makers hope to fly paying passengers by the 2028 Olympics.
paragraphs: Electric aviation is edging closer to everyday use in the United States, as companies race to develop quiet, battery-powered aircraft, PBS NewsHour reported.

In Burlington, Vermont, BETA Technologies designs and builds its own planes, batteries and motors, including a model that takes off vertically. Chief executive Kyle Clark says regulation consumes most of his time, because rules written for turbine aircraft are being applied to electric ones.

Although the Trump administration has scaled back support for electric cars, it is backing electric flight. Under a programme launched in 2025, the Federal Aviation Administration has opened airspace for eight projects across 26 states.
A former FAA official expects commercial services by the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where Archer Aviation will offer 10- to 20-minute air-taxi flights for up to four passengers.

Batteries remain the bottleneck. BETA's plane holds 13,000 lithium-ion cells, roughly five times the energy of a Tesla Model 3, but current technology supports only about five passengers over 150 nautical miles. Investors are cautious too: BETA's shares have fallen around 40 percent since its 2025 stock market debut.
Can a plane fly with batteries? A company in Vermont says yes. It is called BETA Technologies, and it makes electric planes.
Some of its planes can go straight up, like a helicopter. Its boss, Kyle Clark, says the hardest part is the rules. The old rules were made for planes that burn fuel.
The US government wants to help. Eight test projects in 26 states can now fly new electric planes.
Another company, Archer, wants to start air taxis in Los Angeles for the 2028 Olympics. Each trip will take 10 to 20 minutes and carry four people.
But batteries are still a big problem. Today, an electric plane can carry about five people for about 150 nautical miles.
Electric planes are getting closer to carrying real passengers in the United States, according to a report from PBS NewsHour.

In Burlington, Vermont, a company called BETA Technologies builds electric aircraft, batteries and motors. Some of its planes take off and land straight up and down. Its founder, Kyle Clark, says his biggest problem is the rules, because they were written for planes with jet engines.
The government has cut its support for electric cars, but it is helping electric aviation. The aviation agency, the FAA, has opened airspace for eight test projects in 26 states.
Experts expect the first commercial flights by the 2028 Olympic Games in Los Angeles. Archer Aviation plans short air-taxi trips there for up to four passengers.

However, batteries are the main limit. The BETA plane carries 13,000 battery cells, yet today's technology allows only about five passengers over 150 nautical miles. Clark hopes to build a much bigger electric plane within 20 years.
Electric aviation is edging closer to everyday use in the United States, as companies race to develop quiet, battery-powered aircraft, PBS NewsHour reported.

In Burlington, Vermont, BETA Technologies designs and builds its own planes, batteries and motors, including a model that takes off vertically. Chief executive Kyle Clark says regulation consumes most of his time, because rules written for turbine aircraft are being applied to electric ones.

Although the Trump administration has scaled back support for electric cars, it is backing electric flight. Under a programme launched in 2025, the Federal Aviation Administration has opened airspace for eight projects across 26 states.
A former FAA official expects commercial services by the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, where Archer Aviation will offer 10- to 20-minute air-taxi flights for up to four passengers.

Batteries remain the bottleneck. BETA's plane holds 13,000 lithium-ion cells, roughly five times the energy of a Tesla Model 3, but current technology supports only about five passengers over 150 nautical miles. Investors are cautious too: BETA's shares have fallen around 40 percent since its 2025 stock market debut.

Electric aviation is inching towards the mainstream in the United States, with manufacturers racing to bring quiet, battery-powered aircraft into commercial service, according to a PBS NewsHour report.

In Burlington, Vermont, BETA Technologies builds its own airframes, batteries and motors, including a vertical take-off model. Its chief executive, Kyle Clark, says the greatest drain on his time is regulatory, as officials apply rules drafted for turbine aircraft to an entirely different technology.

Paradoxically, an administration that has retreated from supporting electric cars is championing electric flight. The Federal Aviation Administration has carved out airspace for eight projects spanning 26 states, letting companies test uncertified aircraft over three years.
Commercial operations are anticipated by the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, at which Archer Aviation intends to run short air-taxi hops carrying up to four passengers.

Yet energy storage remains the Achilles' heel. Despite packing 13,000 lithium-ion cells, BETA's aircraft can realistically carry only about five people some 150 nautical miles. Markets have grown wary as well, with the firm's shares down roughly 40 percent since its billion-dollar flotation.
Electric aviation is steadily advancing towards commercial viability in the United States, as manufacturers compete to bring quiet, battery-powered aircraft into service, PBS NewsHour reported.

BETA Technologies, based in Burlington, Vermont, develops its own aircraft, batteries and propulsion systems, including a vertical take-off variant. Its chief executive, Kyle Clark, maintains that regulation is the most time-consuming obstacle, since legislation originally designed for turbine aircraft must now be interpreted for an entirely novel technology.

Somewhat paradoxically, an administration that has withdrawn support for electric cars is actively promoting electric flight. The Federal Aviation Administration has designated airspace for eight pilot projects spanning 26 states, enabling firms to trial uncertified aircraft over a three-year period.
Commercial operations are projected to begin by the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, when Archer Aviation plans to offer brief air-taxi journeys for up to four passengers.

Nevertheless, battery capacity remains the fundamental constraint. Even with 13,000 lithium-ion cells, BETA's aircraft can carry only approximately five passengers over 150 nautical miles. Investor sentiment has also cooled considerably, with the company's shares declining by roughly 40 percent since its stock market debut.
